title: Evidence-Gated Autonomous Code Repository Repair for the AMD AI League
surface: AMD AI League — Match: AI-Powered Code Repository Repair

eligibility_gate.note: Registration approval is not a project submission. Re-check the official match window and current submission UI before freezing or filing.

executive_request: Generate and compare three implementable architectures for a high-quality AI-powered code repository repair agent. The system must inspect a repository, identify a defect, propose a bounded patch, run relevant regression tests in isolation, preserve a provenance/evidence trail, and refuse promotion when required checks fail. Evaluate the designs against the same versioned task cohort and identical test/evidence contract. Prioritize verified repair correctness, regression avoidance, reproducibility, and a clear live demo over raw model speed. Keep model-provider calls and accelerator claims disabled unless separately authorized and actually measured.

summary_points.text: The target event includes an AI-Powered Code Repository Repair match; the repository records individual participation only and the current league entry is not evidence of a submitted project.

The repository already has an inspectable repair-PR planner that records incident linkage, sandbox branch, evidence URIs, required tests, rollback SHA, and promotion constraints; its current contract explicitly does not mutate source or create live PRs.
The existing repair design has sandbox planning and verification planning modules, and its repair-PR contract requires repo-gate and termux-smoke among required checks.

The canonical agent-evaluation framework ranks correctness and integrated task outcome above latency and includes deterministic regression, repository-history replay, and patch-quality benchmark families.

The repository's Oracle Method supports evidence-linked proposal generation and a three-candidate cycle with implementation comparisons, equalized evidence, re-voting, and calibration; unavailable stages must be recorded as specified_not_run.

variants.concept: Gated single-agent repair with deterministic safety rails
variants.title: Repair Agent — Gated Single-Agent Architecture
variants.executive_request: Build the smallest credible end-to-end repair system around one repair agent, strict scope limits, a disposable worktree, a bounded retry budget, and mandatory verification gates. The agent may suggest a patch; only the verifier can declare a repair successful. The default path must run offline with fixtures and deterministic test doubles.

summary_points.text: Reuse the existing repair-PR planning contract as the boundary for incident linkage, rollback identity, required tests, and promotion readiness.
Use the existing sandbox and verification planning modules as the starting point, then add an end-to-end runner only where the current code lacks materialization.
Judge success by verified issue resolution and no regressions, not by latency alone.

items.item: Define a versioned repair-task contract and frozen fixture cohort covering known bugs, regression traps, malformed tasks, and no-fix cases.
items.evidence: Exit: fixtures are deterministic, hashed, and include expected behavior and test commands.

items.item: Implement isolated worktree creation, scoped patch capture, path/size limits, and cleanup after every run.
items.evidence: Exit: tests prove isolation, cleanup, and rejection of out-of-scope file writes.

items.item: Implement bounded propose → apply → test → diagnose retry loop with a hard retry cap and stop-on-uncertainty.
items.evidence: Exit: retry budget cannot be exceeded; no unverified patch is marked successful.

items.item: Integrate required repo-gate, termux-smoke, and task-specific tests; emit a machine-readable evidence receipt.
items.evidence: Exit: pass/fail/unknown states reconcile to actual command outputs and exact commit/tree hashes.

steps: Pin the baseline commit and build the frozen task/fixture contract before implementation.
Extend the existing repair planner with an isolated executor and strict patch-scope checks.
Implement bounded repair attempts and test selection; capture stdout, exit codes, duration, and hashes.
Run the same tasks against baseline and candidate; publish per-task receipts and an aggregate scorecard.
Demonstrate one successful repair, one regression rejection, and one abstention in a repeatable notebook/demo.
risks: A single agent may repeatedly make the same mistaken diagnosis; the retry cap and explicit abstention path must prevent loops.
Tests may be incomplete or flaky; UNKNOWN must remain distinct from PASS and a patch cannot pass solely because no tests fail.
Repository-specific commands may not work in the AMD-hosted notebook; define a minimal portable baseline and document any unavailable checks.
alternatives: A multi-agent specialist swarm with independent review.
A retrieval-first repair pipeline using repository history and prior fixes.

variants.concept: Specialist multi-agent repair with independent adversarial review
variants.title: Repair Agent — Specialist Swarm Architecture
variants.executive_request: Build a bounded multi-agent pipeline with separate defect-localization, patch-generation, adversarial-review, and verification roles. Roles exchange structured, evidence-linked artifacts rather than unrestricted chat. A reviewer can reject or narrow a patch, but only deterministic checks and the final verifier can mark it successful. All model calls must be replaceable with local deterministic stubs for reproducible tests.

summary_points.text: The existing repair planner already models evidence URIs, required tests, rollback SHA, and promotion constraints that can serve as the shared inter-agent contract.
The evaluation framework explicitly measures agent trajectories and patch quality in addition to task outcome, making coordination overhead and unnecessary loops measurable.
The system should reuse the existing sandbox and verification planning boundaries rather than granting any agent direct promotion authority.

items.item: Define typed role inputs/outputs for locator, patcher, adversarial reviewer, and verifier; require evidence references for defect claims.
items.evidence: Exit: schema tests reject missing provenance, invalid paths, and unsupported success claims.

items.item: Implement role orchestration with strict step/time/token budgets and deterministic stub providers.
items.evidence: Exit: max steps and retries are enforced; provider-independent tests pass.

items.item: Implement reviewer challenge and patch revision only when a concrete counterexample or failed check is cited.
items.evidence: Exit: every revision has a reason and before/after diff receipt.

items.item: Compare swarm outcomes with the single-agent baseline on the identical frozen cohort.
items.evidence: Exit: report correctness, regression rate, patch scope, abstentions, cost, latency, and trajectory length.

steps: Freeze role contracts and the shared task cohort before adding orchestration.
Build the locator, patcher, critic, and verifier as independently testable functions with stubbed providers.
Add a bounded coordinator that records every transition and rejects untyped or unsupported claims.
Run paired comparisons against the single-agent baseline using identical tasks and test evidence.
Keep the swarm only if it improves repair correctness or regression resistance enough to justify extra complexity.
risks: Multiple agents can amplify shared errors or produce correlated agreement; independent review must include counterexample-seeking, not majority vote.
Orchestration adds latency and cost and may miss the submission window.
Provider credentials, prompts, or untrusted repository content could cross trust boundaries unless tools and context are explicitly constrained.
alternatives: A gated single-agent loop with deterministic verification.
A retrieval-first design that improves localization before any patch is generated.

variants.title: Repair Agent — Retrieval-First Architecture
variants.executive_request: Build a repair pipeline that first assembles a compact, provenance-stamped repository context from symbols, imports, failing tests, recent diffs, and relevant historical fixes. Use that evidence to localize the likely defect, select tests, and generate a minimal patch. Retrieval must be inspectable and bounded; stale or weak matches cannot be treated as proof. The same verifier and sandbox gates apply as in every other candidate.

summary_points.text: The repository-history replay and deterministic-regression families in the canonical evaluation framework provide an existing evaluation direction for measuring retrieval-informed repair.
The repair-PR contract can carry source/evidence URIs, exact baseline identity, rollback SHA, and required checks through the retrieval and repair stages.
The Oracle Method's evidence-reference discipline provides a repository-native pattern for marking unsupported claims as unverified instead of silently promoting them.

items.item: Build a repository context index for symbols, imports, tests, failure output, and recent history with exact source locations and content hashes.
items.evidence: Exit: retrieval records identify file/line or commit provenance and can be reproduced from a pinned revision.

items.item: Implement a relevance-ranked context pack with explicit freshness and a strict token/byte budget.
items.evidence: Exit: deterministic fixture queries return stable ranked results and reject stale/missing source references.

items.item: Use retrieved evidence for fault localization and test selection, then generate a minimal patch under the same sandbox constraints.
items.evidence: Exit: patch scope is bounded and every localization claim links to repository evidence.

items.item: Run ablations: no retrieval, source-only retrieval, and history-plus-test retrieval on the same task cohort.
items.evidence: Exit: results include task success, regression rate, retrieval quality, patch size, and runtime.

steps: Select a small representative task cohort and pin the repository revision used by every retrieval query.
Build a deterministic source/test/history retriever with provenance and freshness metadata.
Add test-aware localization and minimal-patch prompting behind a provider-neutral interface.
Run paired ablations against the same repair baseline and capture retrieval traces with output hashes.
Keep retrieval in the final design only if it produces measurable gains without unacceptable context leakage or runtime.
risks: Historical fixes may be obsolete, unrelated, or unsafe to copy; retrieval is a hypothesis generator, never a correctness oracle.
Indexing can consume the time budget and produce stale results when the repository changes.
Large context packs may hide the relevant evidence and increase model cost without improving accuracy.
alternatives: A gated single-agent repair loop with no history index.
A specialist swarm that independently localizes and reviews a defect.
